approach: Add the normal reaction and the friction force as vectors; friction points up the incline since gravity's pull down the incline is larger than the applied force.

steps.text: Find the normal reaction and the weight's parts along and across the incline.
The weight's pull down the incline is larger than the 30 N applied force, so friction acts up the incline to make up the difference and hold the block in place.
Add the normal reaction, straight out from the incline, and the friction force, up the incline, as vectors using horizontal and vertical parts.
This resultant points mostly upward but leans toward the down-slope side of vertical by about 16°, which is the direction of OB.
steps.equation: R ≈ 85 N, about 74° above the horizontal ground

common_mistakes.text: Taking the plane's push as only the normal reaction, ignoring friction entirely, points along the perpendicular to the incline instead of along OB.
